pillar_reactions.evidence: Understood immediately and agreed without questions — 'Yeah, that's a pretty clear picture' after the training block, and 'Yeah, for sure' to the commitment check that followed. He had already pre-validated the modality himself earlier in the call from a position of expertise: 'I love functional movements... I've always been like a full range... and kettlebell does everything he's talking about.' He also volunteered a competing modality he had rejected on safety grounds — CrossFit — which made the pitch easier.

Agreed without hesitation: 'Yes, for sure.' The rep framed this pillar as needing only 'small tweaks', which matched the prospect's already disciplined intake — high protein, whole foods, roughly 25% carbs, no processed food, natural 12-to-16-hour fasting windows and a 72-hour fast every two to three months. Notably the rep used the pillar to introduce further fasting, including that Trevor 'did one a couple of days ago with the full moon', to a man three weeks from finishing a heavy antibiotic course; neither party connected the two.

Volunteered a strongly positive reaction and tied it directly to his own goal, which is the clearest enthusiasm signal in the batch: 'I'm pretty sure this is what I really want to do, and Trevor actually teaches me, you know, where to start, instead of me wasting my time and not knowing what workouts I do, how much weight I should do, doing it improperly, wasting years of my life, trying to figure it out... because this will be like my bread and butter. So I'm actually looking forward to learning this whole fitness industry with kettlebells.' He also asked an engaged forward-looking question about how often to send form videos.

anchors.raw: I went towards my first show so you always start off as like an amateur and then you do shows... My coach wanted me to go pro, but I was just like, no, I don't want to be on gear.
anchors.note: He has retained a competition coach before and taken that relationship to national-qualifier level, so paying a professional for structured training is an established category for him rather than a novel expense. This is the supportive side of anchoring — a prior habit of buying coaching — and it is part of why no price objection surfaced at all.

anchors.raw: I've been following Trevor and his Instagram page for like two years now. I'm like, wow, this guy actually, you know, knows what he's doing, you know, what he's talking about. Right. Cause I'm in the fitness industry as well. So I understand his background.
anchors.note: Two years of content consumption plus self-described industry knowledge meant he had already validated the provider before the call and needed no proof. He arrived pre-sold, which explains a $6,000 close with zero objections, and it also means the offer's value case was never actually tested here. Worth recording that no price anchor of any kind was stated on this call — no competitor figure, no budget, no comparison.

unmet_demand.want: Assurance that strenuous loaded training is safe while three weeks from finishing a heavy antibiotic course, one week after a PICC line was removed
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep asked once — 'I'm just curious if you are all right with working out... are you okay with working out like that already?' — and accepted the prospect's own lay assessment that he was fine because he has no heart problems. No clinician was consulted or suggested, the underlying infection was never named, and the offer contains no clinical screen or clearance step for either party to invoke.

unmet_demand.want: Resolution of back pain severe enough that he cannot lean forward and must brace on the sink to stand up
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Categorised as a mobility issue and promised to resolve through daily five-to-fifteen-minute protocols. No assessment, no cause established beyond the prospect's own guess about weak hips and glutes, and no referral. The programme has no mechanism to evaluate a 10-out-of-10 pain presentation before loading it.

unmet_demand.want: A nutrition and fasting protocol that accounts for an active course of prescribed antibiotics
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Not addressed. Intermittent fasting and full-day fasts were presented as standard practice, with no reference to his medication, his recent infection or his already-extensive fasting habits. Whether extended fasting is appropriate alongside his treatment is unknown to both parties.

unmet_demand.want: Immediate written confirmation of a $6,000 payment
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No confirmation email reached the prospect before the call ended, after a first payment attempt had already failed. The rep verified receipt through his assistant rather than through the system, acknowledged he could not be certain the card would not be charged twice, and advised the prospect to download the invoice from the still-open page himself.
